e-3055.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
e-3055.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle \sin^3{t}, \:\cos^3{t} \right\rangle$ at an arbitrary point where $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$
e-3055.worked_solution:
For a curve $\mathbf r(t)= x(t) \,\mathbf i + y(t) \,\mathbf j,$ the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by 

$$
\mathbf T(t)=\dfrac{\mathbf r'(t)}{\left\| \mathbf r'(t) \right\|}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $\mathbf r(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{3}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{3}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3{cos}^{2}⁡t(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf r'(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\ \text{ } & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{1} \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

 

In the last step, we were able to remove the absolute value bars because $\sin{t}>0$ and $\cos{t}>0$ for $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf r'(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩}{3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 1
?

Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨1t,t,2ln⁡t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞)?

a
11+t⟨−1,t2,22t⟩
b
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩
c
11+t⟨1,t2,2t⟩
d
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t2⟩
e
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate: r'(t)=⟨-1/t²,1,√2/t⟩. Its magnitude is √(1/t⁴+1+2/t²)=(1+t²)/t². Thus T(t)=r'(t)/‖r'(t)‖=⟨-1,t²,√2t⟩/(1+t²), which is option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve
 $r(t)=⟨\frac{1}{t},\,t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty )?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t),\,z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\sqrt{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+(1)^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}+1+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{(1+{t}^{2})^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{1+{t}^{2}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-1,\,{t}^{2},\,\sqrt{2}t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨1t,t,2ln⁡t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞)?

a
11+t⟨−1,t2,22t⟩
b
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩
c
11+t⟨1,t2,2t⟩
d
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t2⟩
e
11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=⟨ddt(1t),ddt(t),2ddt(ln⁡t)⟩=⟨−1t2,1,2t⟩

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t): ‖r′(t)‖=(−1t2)2+(1)2+(2t)2=1t4+1+2t2=1+t4+2t2t4=(1+t2)2t4=1+t2t2

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve: T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=t21+t2⟨−1t2,1,2t⟩=11+t2⟨−1,t2,2t⟩

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms r'(t)=⟨-1/t²,1,√2/t⟩ and ‖r'(t)‖=(1+t²)/t². Normalizing gives T(t)=⟨-1,t²,√2t⟩/(1+t²), exactly option e. The displayed incorrect submission selected c.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem:
Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve
 $r(t)=⟨\frac{1}{t},\,t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty )?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t),\,z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\sqrt{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+(1)^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}+1+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{(1+{t}^{2})^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{1+{t}^{2}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-1,\,{t}^{2},\,\sqrt{2}t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=4ln⁡ti+(t+4t)j at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞).

a
 1(t2−4)(4ti+(t2+4)j)
b
 1(4t2+1)(ti+(2t2−4)j)
c
 1(t2+4)(4tln⁡ti+(t2−4t2)j)
d
 t(t2+4)(t2i+(2t−4)j)
e
1(t2+4)(4ti+(t2−4)j)
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate to obtain r'(t)=(4/t)i+(1−4/t²)j. Its magnitude is √(16t²+(t²−4)²)/t²=(t²+4)/t². Dividing r'(t) by this magnitude gives (4t i+(t²−4)j)/(t²+4), matching option e.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=4\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+(t+\frac{4}{t})\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+\frac{4}{t})\,j \\  & =\frac{4}{t}\,i+(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{4}{t})}^{2}+{(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{{t}^{2}}+{(1-\frac{8}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{16}{{t}^{4}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{8}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{16}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}({t}^{4}+8{t}^{2}+16)} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}{({t}^{2}+4)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+4)}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{({t}^{2}+4)}(\frac{4}{t}\,i+(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+4)}(4t\,i+({t}^{2}-4)\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=4ln⁡ti+(t+4t)j at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞).

a
 1(t2−4)(4ti+(t2+4)j)
b
 1(4t2+1)(ti+(2t2−4)j)
c
 1(t2+4)(4tln⁡ti+(t2−4t2)j)
d
 t(t2+4)(t2i+(2t−4)j)
e
1(t2+4)(4ti+(t2−4)j)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=ddt(4ln⁡t)i+ddt(t+4t)j=4ti+(1−4t2)j

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=(4t)2+(1−4t2)2=16t2+(1−8t2+16t4)2=1+8t2+16t4=1t4(t4+8t2+16)=1t4(t2+4)2=(t2+4)t2

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=t2(t2+4)(4ti+(1−4t2)j)=1(t2+4)(4ti+(t2−4)j)

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=4\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+(t+\frac{4}{t})\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+\frac{4}{t})\,j \\  & =\frac{4}{t}\,i+(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{4}{t})}^{2}+{(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{{t}^{2}}+{(1-\frac{8}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{16}{{t}^{4}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{8}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{16}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}({t}^{4}+8{t}^{2}+16)} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}{({t}^{2}+4)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+4)}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{({t}^{2}+4)}(\frac{4}{t}\,i+(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+4)}(4t\,i+({t}^{2}-4)\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=cos⁡2ti−sin⁡2tj at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
12(−sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj)
b
2sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj
c
−sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj
d
12(sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj)
e
2(−sin⁡2ti+cos⁡2tj)
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives r'(t)=−2sin(2t)i−2cos(2t)j. Its magnitude is 2√(sin²(2t)+cos²(2t))=2. Therefore T(t)=−sin(2t)i−cos(2t)j, which matches option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡2t+4{cos}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=cos⁡2ti−sin⁡2tj at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
12(−sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj)
b
2sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj
c
−sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj
d
12(sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj)
e
2(−sin⁡2ti+cos⁡2tj)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=ddt(cos⁡2t)i+ddt(−sin⁡2t)j=−2sin⁡2ti−2cos⁡2tj

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=(−2sin⁡2t)2+(−2cos⁡2t)2=4sin2⁡2t+4cos2⁡2t=4(sin2⁡2t+cos2⁡2t)=4=2

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=12(−2sin⁡2ti−2cos⁡2tj)=−sin⁡2ti−cos⁡2tj

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡2t+4{cos}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 ⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩

 ⟨sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩

 13⟨sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives r'(t)=⟨3cos(t),−3sin(t)⟩, whose magnitude is 3. Therefore T(t)=r'(t)/‖r'(t)‖=⟨cos(t),−sin(t)⟩, matching option b.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨3sin⁡t,3cos⁡t⟩ at an arbitrary point where t∈(−∞,∞).

a
 9⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩
b
 ⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩
c
 13⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩
d
 ⟨sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩
e
 13⟨sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=⟨ddt(3sin⁡t),ddt(3cos⁡t)⟩=⟨3cos⁡t,−3sin⁡t)⟩

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=(3cos⁡t)2+(−3sin⁡t)2=9cos2⁡t+9sin2⁡t=9(cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t)=9=3

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=13⟨3cos⁡t,−3sin⁡t⟩=⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=ti+(2−t)j at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞).

a
 11+4t(i−tj)
b
 11+4t(i−j)
c
 11+4t(ti−2tj)
d
 11+4t(3i+2tj)
e
 11+4t(i−2tj)
Submit

decision.explanation: For t>0, r'(t)=i/(2√t)−j and ‖r'(t)‖=√(1+4t)/(2√t). Dividing gives T(t)=(i−2√t j)/√(1+4t), matching option e.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\sqrt{t}\,i+(2-t)\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-t)\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i-\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4t}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+4t}{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+4t}}{2\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{t}}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}i-\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(i-2\sqrt{t}\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=ti+(2−t)j at an arbitrary point where t∈(0,∞).

a
 11+4t(i−tj)
b
 11+4t(i−j)
c
 11+4t(ti−2tj)
d
 11+4t(3i+2tj)
e
 11+4t(i−2tj)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find the derivative of r(t):

r′(t)=ddt(t)i+ddt(2−t)j=12ti−j

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(t):

‖r′(t)‖=(12t)2+(−1)2=14t+1=1+4t4t=1+4t2t

Finally, we normalize r′(t) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=2t1+4t(12ti−j)=11+4t(i−2tj)

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\sqrt{t}\,i+(2-t)\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-t)\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i-\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4t}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+4t}{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+4t}}{2\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{t}}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}i-\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(i-2\sqrt{t}\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The coordinate 4t=4 gives t=1, which also satisfies t⁴=1 and t²=1. Differentiating gives r'(t)=⟨4t³,2t,4⟩, so r'(1)=⟨4,2,4⟩ has magnitude 6. Normalizing gives ⟨2/3,1/3,2/3⟩, matching option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩$ at the point $P(1,1,4)?$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,4)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ ⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩ & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{t}^{4}=1 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ 4t=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, we get $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(1,1,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2t,\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3},\,2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(1,1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

r(t)=⟨1,1,4⟩⟨t4,t2,4t⟩=⟨1,1,4⟩.

{t4=1t2=14t=4.

From the third equality, we get t=1. This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point P(1,1,4) is at the tip of r(1).

Now, we calculate r′(t) and evaluate it at t=1:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(t4),ddt(t2),ddt(4t)⟩=⟨4t3,2t,4⟩r′(1)=⟨4(1)3,2(1),4⟩=⟨4,2,4⟩

Next, we calculate the magnitude of r′(1): ‖r′(1)‖=42+22+42=36=6 Finally, we normalize r′(1) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at P(1,1,4):

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at a Given Point
content.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩$ at the point $P(1,1,4)?$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,4)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ ⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩ & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{t}^{4}=1 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ 4t=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, we get $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(1,1,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2t,\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3},\,2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(1,1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives r'(t)=⟨√3 sin(t),sin(t),2cos(t)⟩. At t=π/3 this is ⟨3/2,√3/2,1⟩, whose magnitude is √(9/4+3/4+1)=2. Normalizing gives ⟨3/4,√3/4,1/2⟩, matching option c.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{3}.$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{4}+\frac{3}{4}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{3}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{4},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4},\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨−3cos⁡t,−cos⁡t,2sin⁡t⟩ at the point where t=π3.

a
 ⟨2,34,−1⟩
b
 ⟨−34,32,2⟩
c
 ⟨34,34,12⟩
d
 ⟨3,32,4⟩
e
 ⟨32,32,14⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find r′(t) and evaluate it at t=π3:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(−3cos⁡t),ddt(−cos⁡t),ddt(2sin⁡t)⟩=⟨3sin⁡t,sin⁡t,2cos⁡t⟩r′(π3)=⟨3sin⁡(π3),sin⁡(π3),2cos⁡(π3)⟩=⟨32,32,1⟩

Now, we calculate the magnitude of r′(π3):

‖r′(π3)‖=(32)2+(32)2+(1)2=94+34+1=4=2

Finally, we normalize r′(π3) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where t=π3:

T(π3)=r′(π3)‖r′(π3)‖=12⟨32,32,1⟩=⟨34,34,12⟩

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms r'(π/3)=⟨3/2,√3/2,1⟩ with magnitude 2. Dividing by 2 gives ⟨3/4,√3/4,1/2⟩, exactly option c. The displayed incorrect submission selected b.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at a Given Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{3}.$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{4}+\frac{3}{4}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{3}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{4},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4},\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨cos⁡t+tsin⁡t,sin⁡t−tcos⁡t,32t2⟩ at the point where t=π.

a
⟨−27,0,37⟩
b
⟨12,0,32⟩
c
⟨−312,0,312⟩
d
⟨−12,0,32⟩
e
⟨312,0,312⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Using the product rule, r'(t)=⟨t cos(t),t sin(t),√3 t⟩. At t=π, this is ⟨−π,0,√3π⟩ with magnitude 2π. Normalizing gives ⟨−1/2,0,√3/2⟩, matching option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2}⟩$ at the point where $t=\pi .$
after.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\sqrt{3}t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{(-\pi )^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}\pi )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2},\,0,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=⟨cos⁡t+tsin⁡t,sin⁡t−tcos⁡t,32t2⟩ at the point where t=π.

a
⟨−27,0,37⟩
b
⟨12,0,32⟩
c
⟨−312,0,312⟩
d
⟨−12,0,32⟩
e
⟨312,0,312⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖

First, we find r′(t) and evaluate it at t=π: r′(t)=⟨ddt(cos⁡t+tsin⁡t),ddt(sin⁡t−tcos⁡t),ddt(32t2)⟩=⟨−sin⁡t+sin⁡t+tcos⁡t,cos⁡t−cos⁡t+tsin⁡t,32⋅2t⟩=⟨tcos⁡t,tsin⁡t,3t⟩r′(π)=⟨πcos⁡π,πsin⁡π,3π⟩=⟨−π,0,3π⟩ Now, we calculate the magnitude of r′(π): ‖r′(π)‖=(−π)2+(0)2+(3π)2=4π2=2π

Finally, we normalize r′(π) and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where t=π:

T(π)=r′(π)‖r′(π)‖=12π⟨−π,0,3π⟩=⟨−12,0,32⟩

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at a Given Point
content.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2}⟩$ at the point where $t=\pi .$
content.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\sqrt{3}t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{(-\pi )^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}\pi )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2},\,0,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
